concept.name: Consolidation
concept.definition: A period during which price moves sideways within a relatively contained range after a prior move, reflecting a temporary balance between buyers and sellers. Consolidations are read as pauses that can resolve into either continuation or reversal; the label describes the pause, not its outcome.
concept.intuition: After running, the market rests — price churns in a band while both sides regroup.
concept.mechanics: Identified as a stretch of overlapping bars bounded by approximate horizontal support and resistance, often with contracting volume and range. Resolution is read from the direction of the eventual range break, ideally confirmed by volume expansion.
concept.failure_modes: Consolidations produce repeated false breaks at their edges before resolving; the longer the range, the fuzzier its exact boundaries.
concept.misconceptions: That consolidation means the trend will continue ('a pause that refreshes'); it can equally mark distribution before a reversal.
concept.example: After rallying from 27 to 64, WorldCom consolidated between 55 and 63 for about five months in 1999 before breaking down through 55 (ChartSchool case study).

citations.source: Wealthsimple — Trendlines: how to identify trends with technical analysis
